title: behavioral-failure-injection-and-recovery-eval-playbook-2026
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook describes a coordinated evaluation and triage workflow for deliberately injecting behavioral failures into the inference stack in order to: (1) validate monitoring and alerting, (2) measure recovery and rollback processes, and (3) quantify interactions between prompts, model variants, and quantization profiles. The target audience is applied ML engineers, SREs supporting evaluation harnesses, and model-onboarding owners.

Goals
- Verify that quality guardrails detect realistic behavioral regressions (semantic drift, hallucination spikes, tone/format regressions).
- Validate that fallback and canary rollout mechanisms preserve user-facing SLOs while failing safely.
- Produce reproducible, annotated failure cases (prompt + context + model variant + quant profile) for regression suites and root-cause analysis.
- Ensure automated rollback and remediation scripts are exercised end-to-end.

When to run this playbook
1) Before promoting a new model or quant profile to Dedicated/Hosted in production.
2) After changes to the serving runtime (attention kernel changes, KV cache updates, batching logic).
3) Quarterly SRE/ML game-day and post-incident drill.

Ownership and roles
- Playbook owner: Applied ML — Maya Chen
- Evaluation harness lead: Eng Eval — Oliver Park
- Regression triage lead: Applied ML — Ria Das
- Oncall SRE: Eng SRE rotation (listed in runbook)
- Release manager: Eng Platform (for coordinating canary/rollout)

Preparation checklist (preflight)
- [ ] Confirm eval harness venv and dataset mirrors are up-to-date.
- [ ] Ensure canary alias and rollback policy exists for the target model.
- [ ] Snapshot production traffic sampling for replay (at least 1000 sessions or 10k prompts depending on workload).
- [ ] Lock the experiment bucket in telemetry to avoid mixing with continuous monitoring.
- [ ] Notify stakeholders via Slack channel #eval-playbook and create a monitoring ticket.

Failure injection categories
1. Prompt-level perturbations
   - Add adversarial tokens, remove instruction prefixes, insert contradiction anchors.
   - Purpose: reveal prompt-sensitive degradation and calibration loss.
2. Context truncation
   - Emulate aggressive context eviction by trimming history or corrupting KV cache keys.
   - Purpose: expose dependency on long-context retrieval and cache stability.
3. Quantization stress
   - Apply a pre-validated quant profile at different per-layer granularity or swap to a fast but less-accurate quant variant.
   - Purpose: measure semantic shift and token-level fidelity loss.
4. Runtime kernel change
   - Toggle an experimental attention kernel or scheduling policy in the runtime.
   - Purpose: confirm that kernel-level optimizations do not break invariants.
5. Latency-induced timeouts
   - Inject artificial CPU/GPU pressure or network latencies at inference nodes.
   - Purpose: force partial outputs or truncated streaming responses to validate graceful degradation.

Controlled experiment design
- Hypothesis statement: For each injected fault, write a one-line hypothesis (e.g., "Applying quant-profile-X increases hallucination rate on instruction-following prompts by >12% within 90th percentile traffic slices").
- Experiment matrix: combine 3 axis — prompt slice (intent/formality), model variant (baseline / candidate), quant profile (fp16 / q4_0 / q8_1) — and keep batch size / routing policy constant.
- Sample size guidance: For prompt slices with >0.5% production weight, target n >= 500 examples; for rarer slices target n >= 2000 synthesized/augmented examples.

Instrumentation and metrics
- Primary metrics:
  - Semantic Regression Rate (SRR): percent of responses failing guided eval checks (e.g., hallucination, instruction-following).
  - Response Format Violations (RFV): schema/JSON failures, missing function calls.
  - Latency tail (p95/p99) and timeouts.
  - Fallback trigger count (how often routing falls back to cheaper or more conservative model).
- Secondary metrics:
  - Token Economy delta (tokens per successful response).
  - Cost per successful call (aggregated by model+quant).
  - User impact proxy: negative NPS samples/flagged safety incidents from the sample.
- Alert thresholds (example):
  - SRR > 8% for a slice over 30 minutes -> auto-escalate to regression triage.
  - RFV > 1% absolute increase vs baseline over 60 minutes -> open hotfix.

Experiment runbook (step-by-step)
1) Prepare dataset and labels
   - Export the selected prompt slices and attach golden-labels or expected-output templates.
   - Create synthetic augmentations if needed to reach sample sizes.
2) Baseline run
   - Run baseline model/quant profile through the eval harness and store baseline metrics.
   - Commit run artifact to the eval warehouse and tag with experiment id.
3) Inject fault (one at a time)
   - Use harness flag --inject-mode <category> and provide injection params (examples below).
   - Start a parallel evaluation run against the same prompt set.
4) Observe and collect telemetry (15-minute windows minimum)
   - Verify SRR and RFV streams are populated in dashboards: /dashboards/eval/failure-injection/<exp-id>.
5) Canary rollout (optional, when injecting runtime changes)
   - Deploy candidate to 5% canary with strict fallback and monitor both functional and infra signals.
6) Trigger automated rollback if thresholds exceeded
   - Rollback policy: immediate rollback on SRR delta > 10% OR RFV > 2% sustained for 10 minutes.
7) Run regression triage
   - If failure is reproduced, follow the triage checklist below to produce an RCA artifact.

Injection CLI examples
- Inject prompt corruption:
  eval-harness run --exp-id exp-2026-041 --prompts prompts/intent-billing.json --inject-mode prompt-corrupt --corruption-rate 0.15
- Switch quant profile for stress test:
  eval-harness run --exp-id exp-2026-041 --prompts prompts/intent-billing.json --model candidate-v3 --quant q8_1 --inject-mode quant-swap
- Simulate partial KV eviction:
  eval-harness run --exp-id exp-2026-041 --inject-mode kv-trim --trim-pattern recent-kv --trim-pct 0.6

Triage checklist (when experiment fails)
1) Reproducibility
   - Re-run the failing sample deterministically with identical seed and environment.
   - Attach the raw inputs: prompt, context, cookie, model hash, quant profile, kernel tag.
2) Slice analysis
   - Group failures by intent, prompt length, username locale, and model-quant combo.
3) Golden comparison
   - Compare outputs against golden responses; attach token-level diffs and attention to misalignments (e.g., hallucination spans).
4) Dependency checks
   - Verify that tokenizer version, vocab mapping, and special token handling are unchanged.
   - Confirm KV cache compatibility across runtime releases.
5) Escalate criteria
   - If SRR spike affects >=10% of a high-weight slice or causes customer-impacting errors -> open P1 with SRE and applied ML oncall.

RCA artifact template (what to include)
- Experiment id and date
- Exact injection parameters and harness command
- Baseline vs candidate metric table (SRR, RFV, p95 latency, fallback count)
- Top 10 failing prompts with annotated golden and candidate outputs
- Quick root cause hypothesis and recommended fix (config, rollback, quant profile exclusion, prompt rewrite)
- Action items with owners and deadlines

Recovery and mitigation patterns
- Automatic: immediate model rollback and routing to conservative variant for affected slices.
- Fast manual: apply prompt rewrite adapters for critical instruction-following flows and redeploy canary.
- Long-term: exclude problematic quant profiles for models serving specific high-risk slices; schedule a follow-up quant sweep.

Integration with other artifacts
- Register produced failing cases in the prompt catalog as labeled counterexamples for the guarded evaluation pipeline.
- Add regression tests to the evaluator CI that replay the annotated failing prompts under the locked quant profile and runtime tag.
- Link RCA artifact to onboarding checklist for the model to block promotion until fixes are verified in the eval harness.

Table: Recommended experiment matrix (example)
| Prompt slice | Baseline model | Candidate model | Quant profiles | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| instruction-following (high-critical) | baseline-v2 | candidate-v3 | fp16, q4_0, q8_1 | focus on hallucination and format |
| long-context summarization | baseline-v2 | candidate-v3 | fp16, q8_1 | test KV-trim injection |
| short Q/A (low-risk) | baseline-v2 | candidate-v3 | q4_0 | spot-check latency, cost |

Postmortem cadence and documentation
- For any P1 triggered by this playbook, the SRE incident owner and the applied ML lead must publish a postmortem within 7 calendar days.
- For non-P1 regressions that still violate promotion criteria, publish a short-form RCA in the experiment artifact and close only when fixes are validated in the eval harness.

Appendix: quick reference snippets
- Minimal eval config (JSON) sample to attach to runs:
  {
    "exp_id": "exp-2026-041",
    "prompts": "prompts/intent-billing.json",
    "model": "candidate-v3",
    "quant": "q8_1",
    "inject_mode": "quant-swap",
    "seeds": [42, 314]
  }

- Pager escalation matrix (summary):
  - Alert SRR>8% for 30m -> notify #eval-playbook, page oncall-applied-ml -> if >10% escalate to SRE P1.
